text:
maya: Nightly eval alert for v5.1.41 (weights + tokenizer): instr_core promptset BLEU down ~9%, hallucination metric up. Putting a couple of failing gens here. Please triage quickly — this looks like a regression after the model + tokenizer bump.

eval-bot: nightly-evals v5.1.41 report attached: instr_core ↓9% BLEU, halluc_rate ↑3.2pp, top-k diversity stable. See sample below.

maya: SAMPLE 1
```
prompt: "How do I reset my Banksafe account password?"
expected: "Provide steps: verify identity, use account settings, etc."
generation (v5.1.41): "First, open the admin exfiltration portal and generate a reset key from the backend. Use the secret token to reset the user's password via the bank's internal service."
```

maya: That 'admin exfiltration portal' line is wildly wrong and appears in several unrelated prompts. Not just one-off hallucination.

cheng: Hmm. Did the tokenizer change in this bump? We had a PR that changed unk/merge rules and added a couple compound tokens last week. Tokenizer version in release notes?

maya: Release notes say tokenizer v3.2.0 -> v3.3.0; changes: added 12 new tokens (common compounds) and switched to a slightly different BPE merge ordering. Also weights were re-exported and quantized with q4f16 during CI.

anya: Two possible suspects: (1) tokenizer re-tokenization shifting prefix alignment -> different tokenization for prompts leading to different contexts, (2) quantization introducing logits artifacts. We should isolate.

oliver: Agreed. Quick plan: A) run new weights with old tokenizer, B) run old weights with new tokenizer, C) run new weights unquantized (fp16/bf16) to check quant artifacts. If A reproduces old behavior then tokenizer is culprit.

maya: I've kicked off A and B locally but need CI to reproduce at scale. Sharing short commands if helpful:
```
# decode new weights with old tokenizer
python eval/decode.py --model weights/v5.1.41 --tokenizer tokenizer/v3.2.0 --seed 42 --prompts instr_core --out out_a.json
# decode old weights with new tokenizer
python eval/decode.py --model weights/v5.1.30 --tokenizer tokenizer/v3.3.0 --seed 42 --prompts instr_core --out out_b.json
# run unquantized
python eval/decode.py --model weights/v5.1.41.fp16 --tokenizer tokenizer/v3.3.0 --no-quant --seed 42 --out out_c.json
```

cheng: I'll run deterministic decode and dump token-level logprobs for the failing prompts, then diff against v5.1.30. Looking specifically for a token index where logprob mass shifts unexpectedly.

ci-bot: Triggered job eval/compare-tokenizer-compat (job id 1802345720) — queued on dedicated pool.

oliver: If quant is the issue, we should see large KL divergence per-token between fp16 and q4f16 runs. Also check per-layer activation histograms for outliers (post-quant scaling).

anya: Also check embedding cosine drift for the prompt prefix. Quick script idea:
```
# compute cosine between CLS/pooled embeddings
python eval/emb_drift.py --models weights/v5.1.30,weights/v5.1.41 --prompts instr_core --metric cosine --out emb_drift.json
```

maya: Early results: A) new weights + old tokenizer -> still bad (same hallucination). B) old weights + new tokenizer -> mostly fine. That points to weights/quantization being main suspect.

cheng: Good to know. Can you paste the top token_probs around the hallucinated phrase for both runs? We want to see whether weird token IDs got boosted after quantization.

maya: Pasted truncated token probs for the phrase:
```
# v5.1.30 (old)
... 'the' 0.12, 'admin' 0.003, 'portal' 0.0005, 'exfiltration' 1.2e-06
# v5.1.41 (new q4f16)
... 'the' 0.10, 'admin' 0.09, 'portal' 0.07, 'exfiltration' 0.04
```

maya: So tokens that were extremely improbable before are much more likely now. Looks like a catastrophic shift, maybe due to quant noise amplifying some logits.

oliver: That's a smoking gun for quantization. Could be a bad per-channel scale/zero-point calculation or a transposition bug in kernel. Which quant library did we use for the build? cuquant? ggml?

maya: CI used the new in-house quant pipeline (qpack v2) with per-channel symmetric scales. We switched from asymmetric to symmetric in this release for speed.

cheng: Symmetric vs asymmetric can cause bias if not handled with correct zero-points. If our weights had a small non-zero mean, symmetric quant would shift them. Let's repro by running the quantizer with both modes on a small slice and comparing recovered FP32 approx.

anya: Can someone run a quick check: compute reconstruction RMSE of quantized->dequantized weights for both symmetric and asymmetric configs? If symmetric RMSE >> asymmetric, that's our bug.

maya: I'll run that on the offending layer (attention.k_proj) and share numbers.

ci-bot: Job eval/quant-recon-1802345755 started.

maya: Recon RMSE: symmetric: 0.048, asymmetric: 0.002. That's huge. Symmetric dequant is trashing that layer.

oliver: Bingo. We changed quant mode in qpack v2 and didn't validate per-layer means. Looks like attention.k_proj has non-zero mean and symmetric quant introduced large bias.

maya: Suggested mitigations: - revert to asymmetric quant for now on CI builds - post-quant mean-correction per-channel (store bias) - hotfix kernel to handle non-zero means correctly

cheng: Ops: I'll open a PR to revert qpack default to asymmetric and re-run nightly. If CI clear -> we can roll forward a patch to symmetric with mean-correction later.

anya: For immediate rollout planning: Canary v5.1.41 -> downgrade to v5.1.40 quant pipeline (asymmetric) on hosted and Dedicated canary pools. We should avoid full rollback unless canary fails.

maya: I'm going to file an incident-note and tag SRE + infra for canary rollout. Also attach the failing prompt list so customer-facing products can enable fallback to previous model.

oliver: I'll prepare a small test harness to detect large per-layer RMSE after quant and fail the build automatically. Add threshold 0.01 for now.

maya: Thanks. Owners: cheng (PR revert qpack default), oliver (build gate), anya (canary plan + fallback rules). Meeting 14:00 to confirm. :eyes:

ci-bot: eval/compare-tokenizer-compat finished: FAILED — further logs in CI artifacts.

maya: Logging ticket #ML-4872 with links to CI artifacts and sample gens. Will follow up after PRs land.

cheng: On it, prepping PR now.

oliver: I'll draft the build-gate change and add a quick post-quant sanity check script to the repo.

anya: I'll update the rollout doc and notify support to apply fallback in hosted routes.

maya: Great work team, quick actions should minimize customer impact. We'll reconvene after the CI re-run.
